speaker: Doctor
text: I'm Dr. Agent, and I understand you're experiencing weakness and fatigue. To help me understand what might be wrong, can you tell me how long you've been feeling this way?

speaker: Patient
text: 33-year-old woman. The patient reports feeling extremely fatigued and weak, especially towards the end of the day, to the point of difficulty in self-care. She mentions experiencing these symptoms currently. The patient has been traveling, hiking, and camping recently and notes having had multiple illnesses in the recent past.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds physically demanding; have you noticed any specific muscle aches, joint swelling, or discoloration in your hands or feet alongside this fatigue?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness and fatigue. I also have Mild diplopia.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The combination of progressive weakness, fatigue worsened by activity, and new onset diplopia is highly characteristic of this neuromuscular junction disorder. I recommend requesting a Comprehensive Metabolic Panel to rule out electrolyte imbalances and a Thyroid Stimulating Hormone test, though clinical presentation strongly points to Myasthenia Gravis.
